stem: Which test is definitive for detecting even subtle strabismus?
explanation: The cover-uncover test is the definitive test for strabismus because it reveals a corrective refixation movement when the fixing eye is covered.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the cover-uncover test directly assesses ocular alignment by observing whether the uncovered eye moves to take up fixation.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the Hirschberg test is a useful screening test, but it is less sensitive than the cover-uncover test for subtle strabismus.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the red reflex test screens for media opacity and retinal abnormalities, not ocular misalignment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because visual acuity screening can identify reduced vision or amblyopia, but it does not definitively diagnose strabismus.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the corneal light reflex test is another screening method for alignment, but it is not as definitive as the cover-uncover test.

source.hint: Identify the procedure that involves obstructing one eye to see if the other eye makes a corrective movement.
